title: Variable-span gating and adaptive pad budgeter
creator: Aisha Rahman
description: Introduce a runtime scheduler component that gates candidate requests into variable-width sequence bands (token-width bands) and applies an adaptive 'pad budget' per micro-batch to reduce wasted padding while providing kernel-selection hints to the serving runtime.
background: Mixed-production traffic exhibits high sequence-length variance: many short chats and occasional long documents. Current fixed bucketing and rigid coalescing either force small batches (higher overhead) or large padding waste. We also observe suboptimal kernel choice on heterogeneous micro-batches; kernels that are optimal for dense uniform lengths perform poorly when lengths vary widely. Prior work explored histogram-driven bucketing and elastic length coalescers, but we still see 10-25% token-cost blowup on bursty workloads and uneven latency tails.
goals: 1) Reduce total padded tokens served per hour by >=12% on our mixed workload benchmark; 2) Lower P95 generation latency for short sequences by avoiding long-sequence contamination of micro-batches; 3) Provide reliable kernel-selection hints so the runtime can choose fused attention / sparse-friendly kernels without extra probing; 4) Operate behind a controlled feature flag with safe rollback.
success_metrics: no increase in P50 latency (>1%) and P95 latency regression <= 5% across models
throughput (tokens/s) neutral or improved under 95th percentile of traffic patterns
end-to-end error rate unchanged and no memory spikes in staging during 72h soak
technical_design: Component overview: a lightweight BandAllocator runs in the request router. It maintains sliding histograms per route/model of observed sequence lengths (prefix+decode) and produces a small set of active bands (variable widths) instead of fixed-size buckets. For each candidate micro-batch we compute: (a) a pad_budget = target_total_padding_tokens / batch_size that limits how many padding tokens we allow to accept an outlier; (b) a kernel_hint vector with parameters {preferred_kernel_family, seqlen_mode, kv_binding_strategy}. The allocator uses a late-binding policy for prefill KV references: short sequences can be late-bound to avoid allocating KV buffers until the micro-batch kernel selection stabilizes. Kernel hints are passed via the runtime RPC header to the worker which will prefer matching kernels but fall back safely.
implementation_notes: Band selection: greedy merge of histogram quantiles producing 3-6 bands per route (configurable); favor narrow bands where density is high
Pad budget: adaptive formula: pad_budget = clamp(alpha * median_seqlen, min_pad, max_pad) where alpha tuned per-model; allows temporary relaxation during bursts
Late binding: introduce a tiny reference-counted KV handle that defers memory reservation until kernel confirmed (saves copies for short sequences)
Kernel hint API: extend runtime request envelope with 'kernel_hint' header (stringified JSON) and update worker kernel-selector to respect hints with a safety timeout of 10ms
Scheduling: micro-batch acceptance now checks (expected_padding <= pad_budget) OR (batch_priority==high) to allow SLA-critical requests to bypass
Telemetry: emit band_id, pad_estimate, kernel_hint_used, and prefill_latebind_success boolean for each micro-batch
acceptance_criteria: Unit tests for BandAllocator histogram quantile plumbing and pad_budget math
Integration test that simulates mixed traffic and asserts padded token reduction >= 12% over baseline harness
New runtime handles kernel_hint header and exposes metric kernel_hint_adherence
No memory/regression incidents in a 72-hour staging soak with canary on 10% traffic
Design doc reviewed by runtime and infra (comments addressed)
test_plan: Local unit tests: deterministic histograms and quantile splits
Simulator: run 72h replay of mixed-prod-sim across 10 seeds and measure padded tokens, latency, and kernel selection distribution
Staging canary: enable feature-flag in staging worker pool with 10% traffic for 72h, monitor memory, CPU, and token-cost metrics
Perf bench: for representative models (redwood-7B, llama-13B-8bit, polaris-70B) measure tokens/s and tail latency on both prefill and decode phases
Chaos tests: inject long sequence flood and verify pad_budget stabilizes and fallback triggers correctly
rollout_plan: Feature gated in router (server-side flag). Canary steps: 1) internal-only testing, 2) staging 10% traffic (72h), 3) production canary 1% (24h), 4) ramp 1% -> 5% -> 25% -> 100% with 4-hour monitoring windows and rollback on regression. Provide kill-switch that disables BandAllocator and reverts to legacy bucketing atomically.
